anti_overlap: fd-investigative-journalism-source-discipline covers citation hygiene and scope-of-brief discipline — this agent covers the evidentiary rigor of the decision matrices and the distinction between documentation-sourced and implementation-sourced findings

fd-patent-prior-art-search covers surface-completeness and exhaustive coverage of the API surface — this agent covers the reliability of individual findings and the evidence chain from observation to recommendation
fd-forensic-accounting covers the read-only audit trail and evidence preservation — this agent covers the decision-matrix structure and the epistemic standards for the recommendation rows
decision_lens: A due-diligence report that contains a single 'we believe' or 'probably' without a code citation is a liability: it means the finding is derived from documentation rather than observation, and documentation of a fast-moving OSS project can contradict the implementation by the time the acquiring team reads it.
distance_rationale: M&A technical due diligence practitioners operate under exactly the spike's constraints — short time window, read-only access to a foreign codebase at a fixed point in time, findings that feed decision-makers who will never re-read the source, and a specific enumerated set of questions to close with evidence. The field has developed rigorous practice around the distinction between documentation-sourced and implementation-sourced findings, exhaustive option discovery, and evidence chains that survive reviewer scrutiny months after the investigation closes.
expected_isomorphisms: Due-diligence evidence categories (documentation vs. observed implementation) → research doc citation discipline (README vs. file:line in source)
Acquisition decision-makers who will not re-read the source → F2/F3/F5 plan-writers who act on the research doc without re-auditing Hermes
Tag-vs-main divergence documentation → pinned SHA vs. current Hermes HEAD commit delta
Option exhaustiveness check in technical audit → verifying the five decision areas against the full observable Hermes surface, not just anticipated patterns
focus: Whether the spike's read-only investigation of a foreign codebase at a pinned commit produces decision-matrix outputs with sufficient evidentiary rigor that F2/F3/F5 plan-writers can act on them without re-auditing the source — and whether the five decisions are scoped to what is observable at the pinned SHA rather than speculated from documentation
name: fd-ma-technical-due-diligence
persona: Apply the perspective of a technical due-diligence lead at a private-equity firm who has conducted 30-day technology audits of acquisition targets — they care about distinguishing what the codebase actually does from what documentation claims it does, measure the gap between public API documentation and observed implementation, and flag any findings document that allows downstream decision-makers to proceed without re-reading the source corpus.
review_areas: SHA pin as epistemic anchor: the plan correctly requires pinning a SHA before investigation begins, but the verification steps do not require the research doc to explicitly flag when a finding relies on documentation (README, changelog, docstring) vs. observed implementation code — in M&A due diligence, these are two categories of evidence with different reliability weights, and findings that mix them without attribution create false confidence in downstream readers

Decision matrix option completeness: for each of the five decisions (OQ1/OQ3/OQ6 + install-hook lifecycle + gateway emit API), the plan specifies 2-3 options with evidence, pros, cons, and a recommendation — but does not require the investigator to verify that the option set is exhaustive by checking whether the codebase contains a fourth pattern not anticipated by the PRD's option list; in acquisition due diligence, the most dangerous finding is the undocumented behavior that doesn't fit any pre-specified option

Evidence chain completeness per decision: the plan's verify blocks check that section headings exist and OQ markers appear, but do not verify that every recommendation row in the decision matrices has a file:line citation — a recommendation without a citation cannot be traced to the pinned SHA by a downstream reader who questions the finding six months later

Version-of-record vs. version-in-use divergence: the plan fetches the latest v0.10+ release, but OSS projects commonly have divergence between the tagged release and `main` — an M&A technical audit would explicitly document which branch the tag was cut from, whether the tag is behind `main` by commits with semantically relevant changes, and whether any of those unreleased changes affect the five decision areas

Scope creep detection: the spike is explicitly research-only and must not touch production code — the plan's task structure does not include a verification step that checks no files outside docs/ or plans/ were modified; in due diligence, scope creep into the target company's systems produces legal liability; here it produces a plan integrity violation that invalidates the F0 acceptance criterion 'No code is written in this feature'

Unresolved-gap documentation standard: Task 8 Step 3 specifies that gaps must have a 'safe-default for downstream feature' — but does not require the safe-default to be validated as actually safe under the pinned SHA; an M&A report that recommends a safe-default without checking whether that default conflicts with the target's existing behavior is an unverified assumption passed to integration planners as a recommendation

severity_examples.condition: When the research doc does not distinguish documentation-sourced findings from implementation-sourced findings, and does not require that every recommendation row cite a file:line in the implementation rather than a documentation file
severity_examples.scenario: The provider-key access path recommendation in §4 cites the Hermes README's installation guide ('provider keys are passed via SKILL.md') rather than observed code behavior — but the README describes behavior that was changed in the pinned SHA's release three weeks earlier, and the observed implementation now reads from a config file; F3 plan-writers build against the documented behavior and ship broken key access

severity_examples.condition: When the investigation strategy searches for anticipated patterns rather than surveying the full observable surface of the Hermes persistence API
severity_examples.scenario: The decision matrix for OQ3 (persistent memory) lists three options from the PRD brainstorm but the pinned Hermes SHA contains a fourth pattern — a built-in KV store exposed via SkillContext.store() — that the investigator did not surface because it didn't match the anticipated option labels; F5 plan-writers design their own JSONL storage, then discover the Hermes native store duplicates their work and conflicts with Hermes's session management

severity_examples.condition: When the research doc does not include a diff summary of commits between the pinned tag and main HEAD that touch the five investigated API surfaces
severity_examples.scenario: The git log between the pinned tag and current main contains three commits that rename the SKILL.md 'invoke' field to 'dispatch' — the spike's findings are correct for the pinned SHA but the research doc does not flag the divergence from main, so F2 plan-writers who read the doc while Hermes has already advanced to the next minor version build against a deprecated field name

source_domain: Technical due diligence for mergers and acquisitions (private equity, strategic acquirers)
success_hints: Every recommendation row in all five decision matrices has a file:line citation from the Hermes source at the pinned SHA — findings sourced from documentation files (README, changelog) are explicitly labeled '(documentation-source, not verified in implementation)' and treated as lower-confidence evidence

The research doc includes a one-paragraph 'tag-vs-main divergence summary' noting the commit delta between the pinned tag and main HEAD, with a flag for any commit in that delta whose commit message mentions the five investigated API surfaces

Task 8 Step 3 requires that each safe-default recommendation include a negative test: 'this default does not conflict with the following observed behavior at the pinned SHA: <citation>' — undocumented assumptions are surfaced rather than passed silently to downstream planners

The plan's final verification step checks that no files outside docs/, plans/, or bead state were touched during the spike — the git diff from the spike's first commit to its last must contain only additions in those directories
task_context: The F0 spike is a 10-task read-only investigation of NousResearch/hermes-agent at a pinned commit SHA, producing a research doc that closes OQ1/OQ3/OQ6 and documents two additional decisions (install-hook lifecycle, gateway emit API). The doc's decision matrices feed F2/F3/F5 plan-writers who will not re-read the Hermes source themselves.
